observations:
All five packages identified in this Torah are fully accounted for within the standard framework of Rebbe Nachman's conceptual structure. No independent domain with 3+ explicitly bechina-linked concepts remains unclassified.

The five packages cover the Torah's complete conceptual map:

1. Package 1 (מִלּוּי בֶּטֶן) — captures the Torah's central bechina: that all self-oriented service, whether toward this world or the next, shares the same nature of belly-filling appetite.

2. Package 2 (מוֹתָרוֹת וְטִנּוּף) — captures the 'surplus and filth' domain: money of desire, unholy children, rotten drop, and filth are all explicitly called aspects (בְּחִינוֹת) of the same reality.

3. Package 3 (צֶלֶם דְּמוּת תַּבְנִיתוֹ) — captures the holy-children domain: holy children, God's image, and the awakening of God's form are all explicitly linked as bechinas of the same divine reality. This is the good mirror of Package 2.

4. Package 4 (חֲזוֹת פְּנֵי ה') — captures the highest goal: beholding and knowing God, embodied in David's declaration 'אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ'. This is the good mirror of Package 1 — where Package 1 is service for self, Package 4 is service purely to fulfill God's will and know Him.

5. Package 5 (מִמְתִים מֵחֶלֶד) — captures the neutral structural category of natural death and the this-worldly person's temporal nature.

Candidates considered and rejected:
- 'מָמוֹן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה' (holy money): The Torah mentions that holy money is very elevated and has many holy aspects (line 8: 'יֵשׁ בּוֹ כַּמָּה בְּחִינוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת'), but immediately redirects to the contrast with worldly money without developing bechina relationships for holy money's components. The Rebbe explicitly defers this topic ('כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר'), so there are not 3+ explicitly bechina-linked concepts in this Torah to form a standalone package.
- 'צַדִּיקִים שְׁלֵמִים' (complete tzaddikim): The text mentions David and like figures as the exemplars of Package 4's ideal, but they are agents/exemplars of the 'beholding God' package rather than a separate domain with their own bechina cluster.
- 'מִיתָה קֹדֶם זְמַנָּם' (premature death by divine decree): The text distinguishes those who die early by God's decree (who receive the world to come) from those who die naturally. However, this category has only two components named (the decree and the world-to-come reward), and their relationship is eitza (death before one's time → merit for world to come), not bechina. It is correctly placed within the eitza flow that links Packages 1 and 5, not as an independent bechina package.
